cases.name: all_empty
cases.note: every collection absent/empty at once — the ten v4 reads without a `|| []` still need the key present

cases.name: legacy_persona_links
cases.note: char A: legacy personaLinks folded to partnerLinks (only partnerId+isDefault survive) then deleted — note the FOLD APPENDS partnerLinks after userId; char B: personaLinks present but partnerLinks ALSO present, so the fold is skipped and personaLinks survives verbatim; char C: personaLinks present with partnerLinks EMPTY ([] is truthy in JS, so the fold is still skipped)

cases.name: partner_links
cases.note: partnerLinks (new format): `{...link, partnerId}` keeps every other key AND partnerId's position; the same partnerId in two links memoizes to one new id

cases.name: physical_descriptions_plural
cases.note: legacy plural array with a row collapses to the singular (and APPENDS the key, since the singular was absent) then deletes the plural; an EMPTY plural collapses to null; the singular path remaps id in place; a null singular is left alone

cases.name: clothing_records
cases.note: a truthy legacy clothingRecords is deleted (shift_remove — `trailing` must keep its place); a null one is NOT deleted

characters.trailing: empty array is TRUTHY in JS

cases.name: avatar_overrides
cases.note: each override is REBUILT as exactly {chatId, imageId} — extra keys are dropped, chatId is remapped first

cases.name: chat_settings_bags_present
cases.note: all three nested bags present with truthy ids — each id remapped in place, key order preserved

cases.name: chat_settings_bags_null_ids
cases.note: the bags exist but every nested id is null/empty — the conditional spreads write NOTHING, so the nulls survive; storyBackgroundsSettings is guarded on its one id, so the bag is not rewritten at all

cases.name: chat_settings_bags_absent
cases.note: no nested bags at all (and a null one) — no key is invented

cases.name: instance_settings
cases.note: all three MOUNT_POINT_SETTING_KEYS remap and are REBUILT as exactly {key,value} (dropping any other column, and fixing the key order); a non-mount key passes through byte-identical; a mount key with an EMPTY value passes through unchanged

cases.name: null_and_absent_scalars
cases.note: remapFields' `typeof === 'string'` guard: null, a number, a bool and an absent key are all left exactly as they were

cases.name: array_field_guards
cases.note: remapArrayFields' Array.isArray guard: a non-array is left alone (it is NOT routed through remapArray's dead [] branch); an empty array stays empty

cases.name: mixed_key_types
cases.note: the keying trap: a UUID array carrying a string, a number, the SAME number as a string, null and true — v4 keys a JS Map, so "5.5" and 5.5 are DIFFERENT entries that collapse to one key in getMapping()

cases.name: repeated_id_across_entities
cases.note: memoization is the whole mechanism: chat.id, memory.chatId, chatDocument.chatId, conversationChunk.chatId and conversationAnnotation.chatId all resolve to ONE new id

cases.name: groups_official_mount_point
cases.note: ONLY the group id is remapped — officialMountPointId is deliberately left alone (groups.create discards it and provisions a fresh store), and groups get NO userId rewrite

cases.name: pass_through_collections
cases.note: providerModels (global) and textReplacementRules (global config, nothing references rule ids) pass through untouched — ids included

cases.name: doc_mount_graph
cases.note: the document-store tables: a file id shared by its document and blob rows resolves to one new id, and every FK is rewritten

cases.name: user_id_position
cases.note: trap 1: an EXISTING userId keeps its position with the new value; an absent one is APPENDED
